claims.statement: Open SWE uses PostgreSQL-backed durable state to coordinate thread-facing mechanisms; `POSTGRES_URI` configures the async PostgreSQL engine.

The PostgreSQL thread index stores a thread's metadata, selected runtime, and status while checkpoints and streams remain with the runtime; per-thread advisory locking prevents a stale sync from overwriting a newer read.

Queued thread follow-ups are individual, ordered durable rows: writers insert rows, a run deletes only accepted sequence numbers, dashboard queue IDs deduplicate retries per thread, and the queue is capped at 100 newest messages with UI invalidation on mutation.

The thread inbox reads queued follow-ups, task messages, and event matches without consuming them, returns receipt identifiers, and removes or marks those items delivered only through `receive`; inbox receipts are accepted both during a later read and through the report endpoint.

Run input is a structured `RunMessage`/`RunInput` contract: builders serialize sender, surface, kind, channel, and structured data into input-message envelopes; system inputs retain notification metadata.
The inbox preserves already-structured queued RunMessages and requires one structured envelope per message because transcript parsing expects one envelope per message.

An event subscription persists an `event_match` before starting a run; nonempty delivery IDs are deduplicated per thread and source, owed matches are read oldest-first until received, and delivery is retried at most three automatic starts rather than relying on a cancellable runtime queue.
Delivered event matches are represented as system RunMessage envelopes with the event-match receipt in envelope data and a stable `event-match:<UUID>` message ID.

The MDA outbox keeps reports in checkpointed graph state, batches them in order, retries until acknowledged, can be adopted by a restarted or later run, and eventually leaves unsent work checkpointed; permanently refused items are dropped after three refusals so they cannot block later reports.

For non-idempotent remote-run reports, backend report receipts are keyed by thread and idempotency key: a claimant records the response, duplicates return that stored response, abandoned claims can be taken over after ten minutes, and retained receipts are purged after seven days.

Transcript `append` is the sole writer and atomically locks a thread, assigns gapless versions, writes events, projections, auxiliary content, command receipts, head update, and notification; a repeated command ID returns its prior version instead of appending again.
Transcript event payloads are typed and schema-versioned, serve as the UI wire format, and keep attachments and full tool output out of the event payload in transactionally associated storage.

Transcript snapshots read projections in a repeatable-read transaction; live subscribers receive only version notifications and reconnect resynchronizes to current heads or deletion, so lost notifications cost latency rather than history.

Webhook `record_once` claims a source-scoped delivery ID before recording, suppresses duplicate logging and subscriber wakeups, releases a successful claim if storage fails, and uses expiring claims that sweep stale entries.
The event log is a daily-partitioned append-only record retained for 14 days, and logging a committed event then invokes subscription delivery.

UI invalidations persist topic rows and publish PostgreSQL notifications in the same transaction; reconnecting readers replay rows within a one-day retention window, conservatively refetch beyond retention or on replay failure, and authorization controls which keyed topics a session can hear.
Focused tests validate transcript receipt/version semantics and keyset paging, UI invalidation commit/replay/access behavior, and webhook retry deduplication rather than only payload serialization.
